title: Compatibility of Concurrent Aerobic and Strength Training for Skeletal Muscle Size and Function: An Updated Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
authors: Schumann M, Feuerbacher JF, Sunkeler M, Freitag N, Ronnestad BR, Doma K, Lundberg TR
population: Healthy adults of any sex and age in 43 studies of supervised concurrent aerobic plus strength training of 4 weeks or more versus identical strength training alone
findings: 43 studies; pooled SMD for maximal strength -0.06 (95% CI -0.20 to 0.09, p = 0.446) and muscle hypertrophy -0.01 (-0.16 to 0.18, p = 0.919): no compromise.

Explosive strength was attenuated: SMD -0.28 (-0.48 to -0.08, p = 0.007), more so when aerobic and strength work were in the same session (p = 0.043) than when separated by at least 3 hours (p > 0.05).
No significant moderators: aerobic type (cycling vs running), frequency (more than 5 vs fewer than 5 weekly sessions), training status (untrained vs active) or mean age (below vs above 40 years).
limitations: Outcomes are strength and muscle size, not running performance; participants were healthy adults, not described as elite endurance athletes; session-separation subgroup rests on few studies; supervised programs.
implications: Separate plyometric or explosive work from key running sessions by at least 3 hours where feasible, or put it on a different day; same-session lifting is acceptable for maximal strength goals.
Do not reduce the strength prescription for masters runners on interference grounds; no age moderation (below vs above 40) was found.
Do not assume running volume blocks strength gains in general; combine with Wilson 2012 for caution at very high endurance volume.

verification.notes: Crossref year 2021 (online-first), issue year 2022. Corrected training-status moderator to 'untrained vs active' per full abstract.
